end.summary:
Vihaan practised the court structure: district court, High Court, Supreme Court, and appeal through easy questions; a why or new-situation question is still to check.
They practised distinguishing civil and criminal cases; some examples were identified, but the distinction was not steady yet.
Vihaan repeatedly mixed up access to justice, saying court cases are mainly for people who can afford lawyers.
They practised that police investigate criminal cases and the public prosecutor presents the case for the state, but the access-to-justice mix-up remained at the last turn.
Lok Adalat was raised but not yet discussed.
end.parentNote: Asha practised the court hierarchy, appeals, and the difference between civil and criminal cases with Vihaan. Vihaan could place the courts in order during easy questions and identified some case examples, while the civil/criminal distinction still needs varied practice. They also practised the role of the police, state, and public prosecutor, but the idea that only people who can afford lawyers can reach court was not corrected by the end. At home, use two or three short examples and ask Vihaan to name the case type and explain who brings a criminal case to court.
